title: PB1.1 - 8 Arnold Avenue - Notice of Intention to Designate a Property under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act

stages.body: Senior Manager, Heritage Planning, Urban Design, City Planning
stages.summary:
This report recommends that City Council state its intention to designate the property at 8 Arnold
Avenue under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act for its cultural heritage value according to
the Statement of Significance and description of heritage attributes found in Attachment 1.
 
The subject property at 8 Arnold Avenue is located just within the northern boundary of the Rockcliffe-
Smythe neighbourhood, south of Lambton Avenue. The residence is notable as a red-brick, one-and-a-
half-storey, Ontario Farmhouse-style property, dating from c.1870s – 1880s, and historically known as
the George Marshall Residence. The property, which is the earliest known house in the Mount Dennis
community, serves to recall the community’s former farming and settlement past. A location map and
current photograph of the property are found in Attachment 2.
 
In 2021 the Mount Dennis Cultural Heritage Resource Assessment (CHRA) was completed by the
heritage consulting firm, Common Bond Collective, as part of the Picture Mount Dennis Planning
Framework Study. The CHRA identified the property at 8 Arnold Avenue as having potential heritage
value for its design/physical, and historical/associative value. The Mount Dennis Secondary Plan and
the associated Official Plan Amendment (OPA 571) was approved by the Ontario Land Tribunal on
October 11, 2024.  
 
City Council listed the property at 8 Arnold Avenue on the City of Toronto's Heritage Register on May
20, 2026.
 
On August 19, 2026, Toronto Building received an application to demolish the dwelling at 8 Arnold
Avenue. On October 14, 2026, Toronto Building issued an Applicable Law Notice to the applicant
identifying outstanding requirements relating to demolition control under S.33 of the Planning Act and
notice under the Ontario Heritage Act.
 
The owner must submit to Heritage Planning a Notice of Intention to Demolish, as required under

stages.recommendations:
The Senior Manager, Heritage Planning, Urban Design, City Planning recommends that:
 
1. City Council state its intention to designate the property at 8 Arnold Avenue under Part IV, Section 29
of the Ontario Heritage Act in accordance with the Statement of Significance for 8 Arnold Avenue
(Reasons for Designation) attached as Attachment 1, to the report, October 28, 2026, from the Senior
Manager, Heritage Planning, Urban Design, City Planning.
 
2. If there are no objections to the designation, City Council authorize the City Solicitor to introduce the
Bill in Council designating the property under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act.

claims.sentence: The property owner must give at least 60 days' written notice to Heritage Planning of their intention to demolish a structure on a listed property.

claims.sentence: Staff found that the property meets three of the nine provincial criteria required for municipal heritage designation.
claims.quote: Staff have determined that 8 Arnold Avenue meets three out of nine criteria in Ontario Regulation 9/06, the criteria prescribed for municipal designation under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act.

claims.sentence: A property may be designated if it meets two or more of the nine criteria.
claims.quote: A property may be designated under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act, if it meets two or more of the nine criteria.

claims.sentence: Designation allows City Council to review proposed changes or demolitions and enforce heritage maintenance standards.
claims.quote: Designation enables City Council to review proposed alterations or demolitions to the property and enforce heritage property standards and maintenance.

claims.sentence: If there are no objections to the designation, staff recommend that City Council allow the City Solicitor to introduce a bill to designate the property.
